title: Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) Unmanned Aircraft Systems Officer (I) (LtCol to Capt) NMOS (7315, 7318), DC AVN
raw_text:
3. MOS 7377, Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) Unmanned Aircraft Systems
Officer (I) (LtCol to Capt) NMOS (7315, 7318), DC AVN

    a. Summary. Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) Unmanned Aircraft
Systems Officers are subject matter experts who train personnel on aviation
unmanned systems for operations in a total threat environment in coordination
with ground and other aviation units.

       b.   Prerequisites.    Must hold MOS 7315 or 7318.

    c. Requirements. Must successfully complete the MAWTS-1 Weapons and
Tactics Instructor Course (M149711) Yuma, AZ.

       d.   Duties

            (1) Manage a unit’s Weapons and Tactics Training Program.

        (2) Perform classroom and operational instruction on various facets
of the equipment/weapons systems.




                                          1-272                         Enclosure (1)
 1142                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



            (3) Analyze performance and provide corrective guidance.

            (4) Instruct on current enemy capabilities and tactics to counter the
threat.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

OFFICERS/OPERATORS

3. MOS 7377, Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) Unmanned Aircraft Systems Officer (I) (LtCol to Capt) NMOS (7315, 7318), DC AVN a. Summary. Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) Unmanned Aircraft Systems Officers are subject matter experts who train personnel on aviation unmanned systems for operations in a total threat environment in coordination with ground and other aviation units. b. Prerequisites. Must hold MOS 7315 or 7318. c. Requirements. Must successfully complete the MAWTS-1 Weapons and Tactics Instructor Course (M149711) Yuma, AZ. d. Duties (1) Manage a unit’s Weapons and Tactics Training Program. (2) Perform classroom and operational instruction on various facets of the equipment/weapons systems. (3) Analyze performance and provide corrective guidance. (4) Instruct on current enemy capabilities and tactics to counter the threat.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
